# Skills-check verification journey

Use this example to check real CLI outcomes with a reusable driver. The default journey covers `healthy` and `missing-ref`. Add `--scope full` to cover all five mapped cases: `healthy`, `missing-ref`, `drift`, `mixed` and `empty`. It creates local Git fixtures, runs the compiled `skills check` command, checks retained evidence, and writes a feature map for the selected scope. An expected negative remains a product failure or drift result; verification does not recover the source.

## Target and prerequisites

Work from the root of the actual OSStack target checkout. Read `scripts/method-verification-journey.mjs` there and record its revision. Exported `.agents/skills/` or `.claude/skills/` directories contain method text, not this script or the compiled product. Do not run repository-relative commands from an exported skill directory.

Use the target's supported Node and pnpm versions, local Git, installed dependencies and current compiled artifacts. In a fresh checkout, run the repository's `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` and `pnpm build` before the journey. Retain their logs separately. A successful build is a prerequisite, not proof of either CLI outcome. If tracked generated files were restored after a build, rebuild them explicitly; incremental cache state alone does not establish current output bytes.

Choose an absolute, owned scratch path with no leading or trailing whitespace. Assign it to the shell variable `OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT` in the script before the block below, or export it from the calling shell. Do not use a project directory, a volume root or a serving home. The preamble below rejects an unset, empty or relative value, exports the selected path for Node, and creates the scratch root and its `runtime` parent directory. The journey output itself must be new. Existing output, including a symlink, is refused. This recipe requires an explicit root; it does not use the wrapper's default temporary path.

## Drive and doctor

Run the following block as a shell script from the target checkout root, with the prerequisites above satisfied. Do not paste its `exit` guards into an interactive shell that you want to keep open:

```sh
umask 077
export OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT="${OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT:?Set an absolute owned scratch path first}"
case "$OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT" in
  /*) ;;
  *) printf '%s\n' 'OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT must be absolute' >&2; exit 2 ;;
esac
mkdir -p "$OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT/runtime" || exit 1
journey_output="${OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT:?}/runtime/skills-check-journey-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)-$$"
node scripts/method-verification-journey.mjs --output "$journey_output" > "$journey_output.stdout" 2> "$journey_output.stderr"
```

The script sets `umask 077` before creating directories and logs. The shell retains invocation stdout/stderr as sibling files ending in `.stdout` and `.stderr`; it does not precreate the journey output directory. Read those logs and the command exit status before interpreting the report. Keep the build log separately.

The wrapper accepts `--output ABSOLUTE_NEW_ROOT` and optional `--scope full`. Omitting `--scope` preserves the two-case journey. Unknown or repeated scope options are invalid usage. Do not add `--doctor`, `--dry-run`, `--case` or `--evidence-dir` to it. It calls the existing skills-check driver's read-only doctor before each case, then drives that case. A failed doctor stops the journey. Doctor does not create a passing behavior observation.

Choose the scope before running the block. For the five-case journey, replace its driver line with `node scripts/method-verification-journey.mjs --output "$journey_output" --scope full > "$journey_output.stdout" 2> "$journey_output.stderr"`. Keep the same scratch preamble and new-output requirement. Do not run both forms against the same output directory.

The wrapper creates only its new output tree. Its children use fixture-only HOME, OSSTACK_HOME and scratch paths. It does not open the default control-plane database. Each case uses its own local Git source and fresh fixture. No daemon, live provider or remote source is required.

## The selected feature map

| Case / scope | Required product observation | Product exit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `healthy` / default and full | One source tracks the owned repository's main ref; its blessed SHA equals the current SHA; output reports up-to-date, no failure or drift | 0 |
| `missing-ref` / default and full | One source tracks an absent ref; output reports `no_matching_ref`; the source remains failed | 1 |
| `drift` / full | One reachable main-ref source has an older blessed SHA than the current SHA; output reports drift, with no unreachable source | 2 |
| `mixed` / full | Three sources retain their distinct healthy, absent-ref and drift observations; failure count 1 and drift count 1 both appear. The failure takes exit precedence; it does not erase the drift | 1 |
| `empty` / full | Zero configured sources and zero failed or drifted sources. This is an empty check, not proof that a source is healthy | 0 |

Each case's driver exits 0 only if its expected behavior, unchanged inputs and cleanup checks pass. A driver exit 0 for `missing-ref`, `drift` or `mixed` means the expected negative was verified, not that the source became healthy. Product exits alone are insufficient: check source counts, refs, blessed/current SHAs and raw per-source output against the fixed case definition.

The wrapper exits 0 only when every selected row and its evidence checks pass. Exit 1 means failure or refusal; exit 2 means invalid usage. Read the exit status and `journey.json` together. A failure stops later work; later rows remain `not_run`, not passed. A row can retain an earlier verified observation while the overall journey fails; check each row's `journey_status` and preserve unknown cleanup as unknown.

## Observe and retain

Read `feature-map.md`, `journey.json` and `journey-manifest.json` in the selected output. For each selected case, read its retained `cases/<case-id>/` evidence: receipt, raw command output, cleanup record and manifest. Full scope adds `cases/drift/`, `cases/mixed/` and `cases/empty/` to the two default directories. The wrapper checks receipt bytes, raw-file hashes, fixed case expectations, required source/build anchors, Git identities and fixture ownership. Retain the invocation stdout/stderr and separate build log. Manifest digests establish consistency; they do not authenticate an oracle or prove the build was produced from the recorded source.

These are full engineering audit records. Some command records include the non-secret fixture environment. Do not hand the full bundle to a model task that forbids reading those fields. Define that task's permitted inputs before use. This recipe consumes full local audit records and does not use or require a projection. The existing `scripts/project-method-journey-evidence.mjs` accepts only the default two-case journey. It refuses a full five-case journey before creating its output directory. Do not drop three rows, rewrite the scope or pass only selected case directories to make that projector accept a full run. Retain all five audit records and report this projection limit. If another task needs a two-case packet, use a separate authorized default journey in a new output directory; do not describe it as a projection of the full run. A projection does not establish native host execution or qualification.

Successful cleanup removes each owned fixture and requires `scratch/` to contain only an empty `smoke/` directory. Evidence stays outside the disposable fixture and survives cleanup. Direct-child exit and fixture absence do not prove termination of every descendant: `descendant_termination` remains `not_attested`.

## Failure and maintenance

Keep the failed attempt. A missing build is a prerequisite blocker; an unexpected CLI result needs diagnosis. Do not rewrite the expected negative or delete a failed row to obtain success. A failed case can have a retained manifest marked unverified, an unsealed directory, or no created evidence. Refusal before the wrapper acquires its output directory creates no wrapper-owned output tree. The shell-created parent and sibling logs can still exist; inspect those logs for the refusal reason. Report that distinction.

Timeout or interruption attempts bounded termination of the wrapper's own direct child. It does not authorize killing similarly named processes or deleting unrelated homes. If cleanup is unknown, preserve the owned residue and report it. Use a new output directory for an authorized rerun after fixing the cause.

Use [maintain verification](maintain-verification.md) when the driver, CLI output, evidence layout or this recipe changes. A complete maintenance pass over this five-case map needs source review and actual drives for all five cases and their evidence paths. Run the journey with `--scope full` for that scope; the default two-case run remains valid partial coverage. A blocked or `not_run` row prevents a complete pass. Even five passing rows cover only these mapped local fixtures, not every source, remote provider, installation, race or global configuration. Reading or exporting this reference does not prove native host selection, model execution, provider qualification or a formal joint gate.

This concrete example adapts the pinned upstream [create/maintain verification practices](sources.md). Apply [the common evidence rules](evidence.md) to each actual run.

# Maintain verification instructions

Maintain a named verification directory and its feature map. If none exists, use [create-verification](create-verification.md). This task edits only its authorized instructions/map/harness; a discovered product regression is recorded, not hidden by a documentation change.

1. Compare the feature index to actual files and current source entry points. Identify missing or duplicate entries and newly introduced user paths. Cite concrete source changes before claiming drift.
2. Read each mapped feature against current code and prepare its shortest meaningful live recipe. Independent source readers can work in parallel when delegation is authorized; one coordinator owns each live instance and serializes drives against it.
3. Run the documented doctor before first drive and after surprising behavior. If a healthy process hides broken application state, reset only owned fixture state or relaunch. Do not repeatedly drive a stale instance because its PID still exists.
4. Exercise every mapped feature for a complete maintenance pass. Keep a per-feature source review and execution record. An unreachable feature needs the attempted route and exact missing prerequisite; it stays blocked or partial coverage, never passed. Broader unlisted coverage remains explicitly out of scope.
5. Classify each issue: **documentation drift** (incorrect instructions), **harness gap** (product behavior cannot be driven or observed reliably), or **product regression** (observed product failure). If the evidence cannot distinguish them, classify as unknown and state the next experiment. Do not lower a predicate, delete a failing feature or omit a required prerequisite to obtain green output.
6. Re-drive every corrected instruction/harness path and preserve earlier failed evidence. Cleanup each failed attempt and the final instance, verifying evidence survives. Unknown process termination prevents clean closeout.

Report one outcome with its coverage:

- **clean**: all mapped features received source and live coverage, required cleanup was confirmed, no correction needed.
- **changed**: authorized corrections were made and their affected paths re-proven; disclose any remaining coverage gaps. Publication follows the user's existing scope, never this label alone.
- **blocked**: a prerequisite, ambiguous failure, unsafe ownership or incomplete required coverage prevents completion. Retain findings and a specific next step.

For partial work, report “blocked, with verified corrections” rather than suggesting the whole map is current. A product regression remains in the evidence even if a separate harness defect was fixed. No recurring automation is created by this method.

The [skills-check journey](skills-check-journey.md) is a concrete five-case target with a backward-compatible default two-case run. For a complete maintenance pass over its map, use the documented `--scope full` option and retain source review plus live evidence for `healthy`, `missing-ref`, `drift`, `mixed` and `empty`. Follow that wrapper's actual interface; do not transfer options from the underlying driver.

The five product exits are 0, 1, 2, 1 and 0 respectively. Also check their meanings: one healthy source, one unreachable ref, one reachable but drifted source, three mixed sources with both failure and drift retained, and no sources. A driver exit 0 confirms the expected observation and evidence checks; it does not turn failure/drift into healthy, or make an empty configuration proof of source health. Inspect per-case cardinality, refs, blessed/current SHAs, raw output, input stability and cleanup. Do not maintain the map by exit codes alone.

The default `healthy`/`missing-ref` run still provides useful two-case evidence. Label it partial when the requested maintenance scope is all five; blocked or `not_run` rows remain missing coverage. Preserve the failed attempt and unknown cleanup when execution stops early. Full completion covers these five local fixture cases only, not all live sources or global behavior. The existing two-case packet projector refuses full-journey input; keep the full audit bundle rather than omit rows or claim that a two-case packet represents all five.

name: CI

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      semantic_provider:
        description: Paid semantic provider smoke to run (manual only)
        required: true
        default: none
        type: choice
        options:
          - none
          - deepseek-no-tools
  push:
    branches: [main, changeset-release/main]
  pull_request:

concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  check:
    needs: graph-macos-fixtures
    if: ${{ always() }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # The integrated full suite takes ~14 minutes before the existing package
    # install / release smokes. Keep their verification, and budget the whole
    # job separately from unchanged per-test and startup latency limits.
    timeout-minutes: 35
    steps:
      - name: Require macOS Graph fixture success
        env:
          MACOS_GRAPH_RESULT: ${{ needs.graph-macos-fixtures.result }}
        run: test "$MACOS_GRAPH_RESULT" = success

      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Classify changed paths
        id: changes
        env:
          PR_BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          PUSH_BEFORE_SHA: ${{ github.event.before }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          BASE_SHA="${PR_BASE_SHA:-$PUSH_BEFORE_SHA}"
          if [ -z "$BASE_SHA" ] || [ "$BASE_SHA" = "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ]; then
            echo "heavy_smoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "No usable base SHA; running full CI smoke." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            exit 0
          fi

          git diff --name-only "$BASE_SHA" "$HEAD_SHA" > changed-files.txt
          if [ ! -s changed-files.txt ]; then
            echo "heavy_smoke=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "No changed files detected; running full CI smoke." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            exit 0
          fi

          heavy_smoke=false
          while IFS= read -r path; do
            case "$path" in
              docs/*|README.md|README.zh.md|CHANGELOG.md)
                ;;
              *)
                heavy_smoke=true
                ;;
            esac
          done < changed-files.txt

          echo "heavy_smoke=$heavy_smoke" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ "$heavy_smoke" = "true" ]; then
            echo "Code or release-sensitive files changed; running full CI smoke." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          else
            echo "Documentation-only change; skipping heavy smoke after lint/build/typecheck/test." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
          fi

      - name: Changeset coverage
        if: github.head_ref != 'changeset-release/main' && github.ref != 'refs/heads/changeset-release/main'
        env:
          PR_BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          PUSH_BEFORE_SHA: ${{ github.event.before }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.sha }}
        run: |
          node scripts/check-changeset-coverage.mjs --self-test
          node scripts/check-changeset-coverage.mjs

      # pnpm version comes from package.json's packageManager field
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: pnpm

      - uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: latest

      - name: Install
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Lint (Biome)
        run: pnpm lint

      # R0.1 release-fact gate: README/package.json/binary-channel version
      # claims must agree (offline mode; --remote is for local/manual audits).
      - name: Release facts
        run: pnpm smoke:version-packages && node scripts/release-facts.mjs --self-test && node scripts/release-facts.mjs

      - name: Clean typecheck contract
        run: pnpm smoke:clean-typecheck

      # Build before test/typecheck: packages import each other via dist/.
      - name: Build
        run: pnpm -r build

      # R0.2 inventory freshness: generated docs/inventory/* must match a
      # regeneration (deterministic script; needs the built CLI for --help).
      - name: Inventory freshness
        run: node scripts/generate-inventory.mjs --check

      - name: Typecheck
        run: pnpm typecheck:check

      - name: Test
        run: pnpm -r test

      - name: Method export contracts
        run: pnpm test:method-export

      - name: Method material pagination contracts
        run: pnpm test:method-read

      - name: Session adoption decision smoke (local fixture)
        run: pnpm smoke:engineering-decision

      - name: Skills check verification (local Git fixtures)
        id: skills-check
        env:
          OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT: ${{ runner.temp }}/osstack
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT/runtime"
          pnpm smoke:skills-check --evidence-dir "$OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT/runtime/skills-check-ci-evidence"

      - name: Preserve skills check evidence
        if: always() && steps.skills-check.outcome != 'skipped'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: skills-check-evidence-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/osstack/runtime/skills-check-ci-evidence
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Method verification journey contracts
        run: pnpm test:method-journey

      - name: Method verification journey (two real local cases)
        id: method-journey
        env:
          OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT: ${{ runner.temp }}/osstack
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT/runtime"
          pnpm smoke:method-journey --output "$OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT/runtime/method-journey-ci-evidence"

      - name: Preserve method journey evidence
        if: always() && steps.method-journey.outcome != 'skipped'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: method-journey-evidence-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/osstack/runtime/method-journey-ci-evidence
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Full method verification journey (five real local cases)
        id: method-journey-full
        env:
          OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT: ${{ runner.temp }}/osstack
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT/runtime"
          pnpm smoke:method-journey --output "$OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT/runtime/method-journey-full-ci-evidence" --scope full

      - name: Preserve full method journey evidence
        if: always() && steps.method-journey-full.outcome != 'skipped'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: method-journey-full-evidence-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/osstack/runtime/method-journey-full-ci-evidence
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 7

      - name: Model evidence projection contracts
        env:
          OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT: ${{ runner.temp }}/osstack
        run: pnpm test:method-projection

      - name: Project and check actual method evidence
        id: method-projection
        env:
          OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT: ${{ runner.temp }}/osstack
        run: |
          pnpm method:project-evidence --input "$OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT/runtime/method-journey-ci-evidence" --output "$OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT/runtime/method-packet-ci-evidence"
          pnpm method:project-evidence --check "$OSSTACK_SCRATCH_ROOT/runtime/method-packet-ci-evidence"

      - name: Preserve model evidence packet
        if: always() && steps.method-projection.outcome != 'skipped'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4
        with:
          name: method-packet-evidence-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/osstack/runtime/method-packet-ci-evidence
          if-no-files-found: warn
          retention-days: 7

      # Startup budget gate: median-of-5 spawns of the built dist/bin.js.
      # Budgets are looser than the local defaults (150/500ms) because CI
      # runners spawn node slower; they still catch the eager-import class
      # of regression (each costs 100ms+). See scripts/bench-cli-startup.mjs.
      - name: CLI startup budget
        env:
          OSSTACK_BENCH_VERSION_BUDGET_MS: "250"
          OSSTACK_BENCH_HELP_BUDGET_MS: "900"
        run: node scripts/bench-cli-startup.mjs

      - name: Neat semantic live diagnostic tests
        run: pnpm test:neat-semantic-live-diagnostic

      - name: Neat semantic beta contract gates
        if: steps.changes.outputs.heavy_smoke == 'true'
        run: |
          pnpm smoke:neat
          pnpm eval:neat-goldens
          pnpm eval:neat-parity:corpus
          pnpm eval:neat-parity:offline

      # DeepSeek ds-review/ds-verify evaluation-spec protocol. Stdlib-only
      # unittest (no pip needed); ubuntu-latest ships python3. Guards against
      # regressions in legacy-python/deepseek/lib/evaluation_specs.py that the
      # JS suite cannot see.
      - name: Python protocol tests
        run: python3 -m unittest discover legacy-python/deepseek/tests

      - name: Release plan smoke
        if: steps.changes.outputs.heavy_smoke == 'true'
        run: pnpm smoke:release-plan

      - name: Knowledge Cloud smoke
        if: steps.changes.outputs.heavy_smoke == 'true'
        run: pnpm smoke:knowledge-cloud

      - name: Knowledge Cloud deploy asset smoke
        if: steps.changes.outputs.heavy_smoke == 'true'
        run: pnpm smoke:knowledge-cloud:deploy

      - name: Deliver proof smoke
        if: steps.changes.outputs.heavy_smoke == 'true'
        run: pnpm smoke:deliver-proof

      - name: Real repo deliver smoke
        if: steps.changes.outputs.heavy_smoke == 'true'
        run: pnpm smoke:real-repo-deliver

      - name: NPM preflight smoke
        if: steps.changes.outputs.heavy_smoke == 'true'
        run: pnpm smoke:npm-preflight

      - name: NPM Trusted Publisher preflight smoke
        if: steps.changes.outputs.heavy_smoke == 'true'
        run: pnpm smoke:npm-trust

      - name: NPM broken release deprecation smoke
        if: steps.changes.outputs.heavy_smoke == 'true'
        run: pnpm smoke:npm-deprecation

      - name: NPM install smoke
        if: steps.changes.outputs.heavy_smoke == 'true'
        run: pnpm smoke:npm-install

      - name: NPM package artifact smoke
        if: steps.changes.outputs.heavy_smoke == 'true'
        run: pnpm smoke:npm-package-artifacts

      - name: NPM publish ordering smoke
        if: steps.changes.outputs.heavy_smoke == 'true'
        run: pnpm smoke:npm-publish-order

      - name: NPM registry skew smoke
        if: steps.changes.outputs.heavy_smoke == 'true'
        run: pnpm smoke:npm-registry-skew

  paid_deepseek_semantic:
    name: Paid DeepSeek semantic smoke
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.semantic_provider == 'deepseek-no-tools'
    permissions:
      contents: read
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: 22
          cache: pnpm

      - name: Install
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build semantic CLI
        run: pnpm --filter @osstack/cli... build

      - name: Verify sanitized diagnostics
        run: pnpm test:neat-semantic-live-diagnostic

      - name: Run sanitized DeepSeek smoke
        env:
          DEEPSEEK_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY }}
          OSSTACK_NEAT_DEEPSEEK_MODEL: ${{ vars.OSSTACK_NEAT_DEEPSEEK_MODEL }}
        run: node scripts/smoke-neat-semantic-live.mjs --provider deepseek-no-tools

  graph-macos-fixtures:
    runs-on: macos-14
    timeout-minutes: 15
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node: ['22', '24']
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm --filter @osstack/cli... build
      # /tmp is an alias on macOS. Fixtures must canonicalize their roots;
      # production path-identity guards must continue rejecting substitutions.
      - name: Graph fixtures through macOS temporary-path alias
        env:
          TMPDIR: /tmp
          OSSTACK_HOME: ${{ runner.temp }}/graph-macos-fixtures-home
        run: |
          pnpm --filter @osstack/graph exec vitest run src/functional-entry.test.ts
          pnpm --filter @osstack/cli exec vitest run src/graph-action-freeze.test.ts src/graph-contained-recovery.test.ts src/graph-delivery-adversarial.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

  graph-runtime-matrix:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        node: ['20.6.0', '22.23.1']
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - uses: pnpm/action-setup@v6
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: '22.23.1'
          cache: pnpm
      - run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
      - run: pnpm build
      # pnpm 11 is a build tool requiring recent Node; exercise the runtime
      # directly under the declared minimum with its matching SQLite ABI.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node }}
      - run: npm install --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/graph-gyp" node-gyp@11.5.0
      - name: Test bounded Node header preparation
        run: node --test scripts/prepare-node-headers.test.mjs
      - name: Prepare verified runtime headers
        timeout-minutes: 8
        run: |
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/osstack/runtime"
          node scripts/prepare-node-headers.mjs --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/osstack/runtime/graph-node-headers"
      - name: Build SQLite for runtime ABI
        run: |
          cd "$(node -p 'require("node:path").dirname(require.resolve("better-sqlite3/package.json", {paths:["./packages/core"]}))')"
          node "$RUNNER_TEMP/graph-gyp/node_modules/node-gyp/bin/node-gyp.js" rebuild --release --nodedir="$RUNNER_TEMP/osstack/runtime/graph-node-headers/node-v$(node -p process.versions.node)"
      - name: Graph worker and durable SQLite runtime
        env:
          OSSTACK_HOME: ${{ runner.temp }}/graph-runtime-home
          TMPDIR: /tmp
        run: node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run packages/graph/src packages/core/src/state/graph-migration-lineage.test.ts packages/core/src/state/graph-checkpoints.test.ts packages/cli/src/graph-worker-manager.test.ts packages/cli/src/graph-rpc.test.ts packages/cli/src/graph-compatibility.integration.test.ts --maxWorkers=1

# Full five-case verification journey

The existing user journey covered only healthy and missing-ref even though its driver supported three more outcomes. Add `--scope full` to run healthy, missing-ref, drift, mixed and empty in that order. Default calls still use the existing pair and remain compatible with the unchanged evidence projector.

Each row checks raw CLI output, source cardinality, fixture Git old/current SHAs, source refs/blessed SHAs, unchanged input, receipt consistency and cleanup claims. Product exits are 0/1/2/1/0; a verified negative is not a healthy source. Empty means no source was checked. Failure stops later rows, preserving failed/not_run/unknown distinctions and raw records. Full means these five local cases, not all possible product behavior.

+# Full five-case verification journey
+
+The existing user journey covered only healthy and missing-ref even though its driver supported three more outcomes. Add `--scope full` to run healthy, missing-ref, drift, mixed and empty in that order. Default calls still use the existing pair and remain compatible with the unchanged evidence projector.
+
+Each row checks raw CLI output, source cardinality, fixture Git old/current SHAs, source refs/blessed SHAs, unchanged input, receipt consistency and cleanup claims. Product exits are 0/1/2/1/0; a verified negative is not a healthy source. Empty means no source was checked. Failure stops later rows, preserving failed/not_run/unknown distinctions and raw records. Full means these five local cases, not all possible product behavior.
+
+The existing two-case projection deliberately rejects the five-case result before creating its packet. A separately queued full-scope projection is needed for a model-safe five-row packet; this PR does not drop rows or broaden the old contract. No model/host task, provider, daemon or new method is introduced. Four entries and fourteen methods remain unchanged.
+
+Use the actual checkout and supported build prerequisites in `osstack-methods-skill/references/skills-check-journey.md`. The CI keeps the default pair and projection checks and adds an independent full-journey run and retained artifact. Task card `card_ddf5e661` contributes to PS08/PS09, primary J03, supporting J06/J09. Formal joint qualification stays false.
+
+## Verification scope
+
+Author code `32a9a9e1` and docs `08c48fcb` are composed at root `6e4c6168`. Root standalone tests pass 186/186: 43 journey, 49 projection and 94 exporter contracts. The independent FJ01–10 criteria were frozen before author implementation; raw first failures are retained. Author actual full/default runs and unchanged projector outcomes are recorded with working-byte hashes, not retroactively relabeled as commit runs. Actual Claude CLI `claude-sonnet-5-5` static review returned PASS with optional suggestions; original input, response and source bindings are retained. Independent verification on the composed candidate passed: actual default and full journeys, seven source/receipt/cleanup records, 30 bounded interface/adversarial observations, and four failure seams. The original two-case projector succeeds on default output and refuses full output without writing or changing its input. This independently covers the actual-run suggestions in the static audit.
+
+Package sources, package manifests and dependencies are unchanged from the immediately preceding 7,144-pass/5-skip package regression. That run keeps its original 14853→969da2df scope and fresh-dist limitations; it is not claimed to cover this new standalone implementation. Relevant standalone and actual journey checks cover this change, while published-head CI supplies a new full regression before Ready. No additional local whole-package rerun is attributed to this slice.
+
+241 design checks and one documentation hygiene test passed. Retained failures include the author’s initial TDD failures, one test reason expectation corrected without lowering behavior assertions, and an invalid build-command flag before the successful normal build. These are recorded separately from product failures. No source correction was required by the final audit or independent review.

+# pstack-first feature queue
+
+This is the delivery queue, separate from activity counts and the 32 formal joint milestones. Main has four entry points and fourteen method materials; those counts are not completed capability counts. The 24 source capability groups currently contain 20 partially delivered and four deferred groups. No whole-capability completion is inferred.
+
+## Active delivery
+
+| Order | User-visible outcome | Current action | Completion boundary |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| 1 | Read the complete selected method material without silently losing its tail | PR303: bounded paging and digest-pinned continuation; CI pending | Tool contract + actual exported-byte reassembly; model consumption still requires a fresh host task |
+| 2 | Run the full five-case skills-check journey and maintain all mapped cases | card_ddf5e661: add optional `--scope full`; retain default two-case compatibility | Actual five outcomes 0/1/2/1/0, semantic receipts, cleanup limits, default projection compatibility and failure-path verification |
+| 3 | Give a host the complete five-case result without unrelated fixture fields | Queued explicit full-scope projection, preserving the two-case contract | All five cases and failed/not_run/unknown states preserved; original records unchanged |
+| 4 | Use current method materials to complete a fresh actual host task | Next after the tool slice: choose distinct task and freeze fresh inputs/resources once | Codex/Claude actual commands, behavioral RED/fix/GREEN and complete required material delivery; no rerunning old failures for a better grade |
+| 5 | Make PR candidate status easier to assess | Later bounded read-only forge/candidate reconciliation | Head/base/CI/review observations explicitly bound and refreshed; no automatic approval or merge |
+
+Firstmate deep recovery/supervision is deferred behind these pstack paths except for necessary dependencies. Formal identity issue287 does not block ordinary bounded D2a tools.
+
+## Source capability inventory
+

+# Full five-case verification journey
+
+The existing user journey covered only healthy and missing-ref even though its driver supported three more outcomes. Add `--scope full` to run healthy, missing-ref, drift, mixed and empty in that order. Default calls still use the existing pair and remain compatible with the unchanged evidence projector.
+
+Each row checks raw CLI output, source cardinality, fixture Git old/current SHAs, source refs/blessed SHAs, unchanged input, receipt consistency and cleanup claims. Product exits are 0/1/2/1/0; a verified negative is not a healthy source. Empty means no source was checked. Failure stops later rows, preserving failed/not_run/unknown distinctions and raw records. Full means these five local cases, not all possible product behavior.
+
+The existing two-case projection deliberately rejects the five-case result before creating its packet. A separately queued full-scope projection is needed for a model-safe five-row packet; this PR does not drop rows or broaden the old contract. No model/host task, provider, daemon or new method is introduced. Four entries and fourteen methods remain unchanged.
+
+Use the actual checkout and supported build prerequisites in `osstack-methods-skill/references/skills-check-journey.md`. The CI keeps the default pair and projection checks and adds an independent full-journey run and retained artifact. Task card `card_ddf5e661` contributes to PS08/PS09, primary J03, supporting J06/J09. Formal joint qualification stays false.
+
+## Verification scope
+
+Author code `32a9a9e1` and docs `08c48fcb` are composed at root `6e4c6168`. Root standalone tests pass 186/186: 43 journey, 49 projection and 94 exporter contracts. The independent FJ01–10 criteria were frozen before author implementation; raw first failures are retained. Author actual full/default runs and unchanged projector outcomes are recorded with working-byte hashes, not retroactively relabeled as commit runs. Actual Claude CLI `claude-sonnet-5-5` static review returned PASS with optional suggestions; original input, response and source bindings are retained. Independent verification on the composed candidate passed: actual default and full journeys, seven source/receipt/cleanup records, 30 bounded interface/adversarial observations, and four failure seams. The original two-case projector succeeds on default output and refuses full output without writing or changing its input. This independently covers the actual-run suggestions in the static audit.
+
+Package sources, package manifests and dependencies are unchanged from the immediately preceding 7,144-pass/5-skip package regression. That run keeps its original 14853→969da2df scope and fresh-dist limitations; it is not claimed to cover this new standalone implementation. Relevant standalone and actual journey checks cover this change, while published-head CI supplies a new full regression before Ready. No additional local whole-package rerun is attributed to this slice.
+
+241 design checks and one documentation hygiene test passed. Retained failures include the author’s initial TDD failures, one test reason expectation corrected without lowering behavior assertions, and an invalid build-command flag before the successful normal build. These are recorded separately from product failures. No source correction was required by the final audit or independent review.
